evidence: src/application/ports/IdGenerator.ts declares the port `interface IdGenerator { next(): string }`. CreateProjectService, AddTaskService and CreateUserService inject it through their constructors, and UuidIdGenerator implements it.

src/application/shared/requireFound.ts: `requireFound<T>(lookup, entity, id)` throws `new NotFoundError(entity, id)` from the domain, so it reuses the domain error rather than defining a parallel one. AddTaskService, AssignTaskService, CompleteTaskService and ListTasksService reuse it.

src/application/errors/ErrorClassifier.ts: `classifyError` maps ValidationError, NotFoundError and ConflictError to `ErrorCategory`. This is the only place the mapping happens, and errorHandler consumes it.
Neither unit file duplicates the other's logic: requireFound only raises NotFoundError and ErrorClassifier only classifies it, with no overlapping invariant.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
This unit is the shared support code of the application layer. It holds an outbound port (IdGenerator), a helper that turns a missing entity into a domain error (requireFound), and a mapper from domain errors to transport-neutral categories (ErrorClassifier). The three files cover different topics, but each one is a cross-cutting application-layer support piece that the use-case services or adapters consume. That is the expected job of the application layer's shared or ports area, not a mix of unrelated business concerns.

No rule is duplicated. requireFound only throws NotFoundError, and only ErrorClassifier maps NotFoundError to 'not-found', so each piece of logic lives in one place. Both error files use the domain's error classes (ValidationError, NotFoundError, ConflictError) instead of defining their own error types, so neither one bypasses the shared abstraction.

The graph shows consistent use. Services inject IdGenerator through constructors, UuidIdGenerator implements it, four task services reuse requireFound, and errorHandler relies on classifyError. Nothing indicates that a local abstraction is being bypassed.

This passes with only moderate confidence because the files sit in different subfolders (errors, ports, shared) and are related only loosely. Still, the rubric does not show a split into unrelated concerns, duplication, or a bypass.
